questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How long it takes to travel to the Sun
Why science fiction films show little green men
Whether a faraway planet might have conditions for life
How astronauts live on the Moon
questions.why: They learn from experts whether the conditions for life exist on a planet 40 light years away.

questions.q: Do Neil and Becca agree about life beyond Earth?
options: Yes, they both think life may exist, but not like in films
No, Neil believes in aliens but Becca doesn't
No, Becca believes in aliens but Neil doesn't
Yes, they both think we are alone in the universe
questions.why: Neil thinks we cannot be alone, and Becca agrees, though 'maybe not as we see in alien movies'.

questions.q: How does Caroline Steele describe TRAPPIST-1e?
options: A gas planet many times bigger than Earth
A small planet in our own solar system
A rocky, Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone
A frozen moon with no atmosphere around it
questions.why: She says it's rocky like Earth, a similar size, and in the habitable zone around its sun.

questions.q: How far from Earth is the planet they discuss?
options: About 4 light years
About 170 light years
Just beyond the Sun
About 40 light years
questions.why: Neil says the planet is 40 light years away.

questions.q: Why is it good news that the planet's atmosphere is not full of hydrogen or carbon dioxide?
options: Those gases would make the planet very hot
Those gases are needed for water
Those gases make planets too cold
Those gases block telescopes
questions.why: Caroline says they're greenhouse gases, which would make the planet really hot.

questions.q: What clue suggests there could be life on TRAPPIST-1e?
options: Signs of liquid water on its rocky surface
Signs that its air may be mostly nitrogen
Radio signals coming from the planet
Clear photos of plants growing there
questions.why: She says there are small clues it might be a nitrogen-dominated atmosphere, a clue for life.

questions.q: What does Caroline think scientists will do next?
options: Send a team of astronauts to the planet
Stop studying the planet and look elsewhere
Look for other planets in our own galaxy
Study other gases and model its temperature
questions.why: She guesses they'll look at other gases and use models to work out how warm the planet could be.

questions.q: What does Caroline suggest when she says 'fingers crossed it has nitrogen'?
options: She is completely sure the planet has nitrogen
She hopes so, as it could keep it warm enough
She thinks nitrogen would be dangerous for life
She doesn't really believe the new research
questions.why: She hopes there's enough nitrogen 'to keep the planet a decent temperature', one step closer to life.
